protocol.source_text:
CLINICAL FEATURES 
* Hypotension, bradycardia, hyperglycaemia (CCB) hypoglycaemia (BB), acidosis, 
CNS depression 
 
ECG FEATURES (see Tox ECG appendix) 
* Sinus bradycardia, AV blocks, junctional bradycardia, ventricular bradycardia 
 
NOTE: 
• 
Propranolol: Also acts as a Na channel blocker – TCA-like features of OD 
• 
Sotalol: Blocks myocardial K channels – QT prolongation, Torsades 
 
 
 
SPECIFIC MANAGEMENT 
*Enhanced elimination: Consider activated charcoal 50g via NGT 
*Haemodynamic support: Fluid bolus, high dose inotropes may be required  
*Airway support: Beta blocker OD may lead to profound CNS depression 
*Specific therapy: 
• 
HIET – see protocol 
• 
Calcium chloride 10 ml 10% over 10 minutes via large bore IV or central line (target Ca 
2mmol) 
• 
Consider Intralipid & glucagon – specialist consultation 
• 
Consider ECMO if no response to HIET – specialist consultation 
HIGH DOSE INSULIN EUGLYCAEMIC THERAPY 
(HIET) 
* Start with a 50ml 50% dextrose bolus 
* Insulin loading dose: 
■ 
Actrapid 1 IU/kg (ie 60-80 units) IV stat 
* Infusion: 
■ 
 Actrapid 0.5 IU/kg/hr, titrate up every 30 
minutes to a max dose of 10 IU/kg/hr IV 
*Dextrose infusion: 
■ 
Maintenance @ 25g/hr 
(50ml 50% dextrose/hr or 100ml 25% dextrose) via central 
line to maintain euglycemia 
*  Monitor HGT every 20 minutes for 1st hour, then every 1 
hour 
* Monitor Potassium – replace if < 2.5 mmol 
THERAPEUTIC ENDPOINTS: 
■ 
EF > 50%; SBP > 90mmHg 
■ 
Adequate heart rate (> 60 bpm) 
■ 
Resolution of acidaemia; euglycaemia 
■ 
Urine output 1-2ml/kg/hr 
■ 
Reverse cardiac conduction Abns - QRS < 120ms 
■ 
Improved GCS 
■ 
Able to wean inotropic support 
 
 
DISPOSITION 
* Int med consult (consider renal consult – dialysis) 
* Will likely require ICU/High care 
* Continue serial ECG and VBG monitoring in ED 
GENERAL APPROACH (see also general toxicology approach) 
•
Triage to RESUS AREA, even if patient initially appears well 
•
Rapid ABC assessment, 2 IV lines, monitors, HGT, VBG, urine
